How the rules were implemented:

- `pieces_at_depth`: converts cm to depth via `from_m + cm/100`, keeps break flags, clips to `[from_m, to_m]`, and drops pieces starting at or after `to_m`.
- `log_hole` validates (non-empty runs, positive finite `step_m`, `zone_min_intervals >= 1`, finite run depths with `to_m > from_m`), then:
  - `boxes`: one `(box, from_m, to_m)` per box from its runs as given, sorted by `from_m`.
  - `issues`: adjacent boxes give a `gap` when the next starts more than `DEPTH_TOL_M` after the previous end, an `overlap` (next start to earlier end) when it starts more than `DEPTH_TOL_M` before.
  - Overlaps: later boxes are cut to start at the earlier coverage end (running max), pieces clipped, emptied runs dropped; never raises.
  - `runs`: consecutive parts that are both `complete=False`, in different boxes, and contiguous within tolerance are joined; every run is logged by converting its depth pieces to cm-from-start `Piece`s and calling `log_interval`.
  - `intervals`: contiguous boxes merged into stretches (gaps split), grid cells at multiples of `step_m` cut to each stretch, slivers shorter than tolerance skipped; pieces crossing a boundary are cut with the cut keeping no flag, then `log_interval`.
  - `zones`: maximal runs of at least `zone_min_intervals` consecutive contiguous intervals with `rqd_pct < zone_max_rqd`; zone RQD is length-weighted (`Σrqd_cm / Σrun_length_cm × 100`).
